title: Economic globalization
summary: On 30 October 1947, 23 countries signed the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, with 45,000 tariff concessions affecting about one fifth of world trade. It provided rules for much of world trade until the World Trade Organization replaced it in 1995. The IMF says world income per person grew almost five-fold in the 20th century, fastest in the second half, a period of rapid trade expansion.

uncertainty.note: Accelerated after the 1947 GATT negotiations and 1944 Bretton Woods agreements; ongoing process through the twentieth century and into the twenty-first.

where.modern_name: Worldwide; stand-in pin at Geneva, Switzerland
where.historical_name: Geneva, Switzerland (seat of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade)

importance.justification: Trade rules and growing exchange tied national economies more closely together worldwide.

related.because: The Bretton Woods monetary conference created the IMF and World Bank, establishing the financial architecture for postwar international economic integration.
Deep cross-border financial integration and globalized capital markets transmitted mortgage debt collapse into a worldwide economic crisis.
